hints: The repeated factor $x^2$ requires terms $A/x+B/x^2$, together with $C/(3x+2)$.
Clear denominators, use $x=0$ and $x=-2/3$ where helpful, then compare a remaining coefficient to determine all three constants.
walkthrough:
State the partial fraction decomposition for a repeated linear factor $x^2$ and a linear factor $3x + 2$:
$$\dfrac{3x^2 - 4}{x^2(3x + 2)} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{x^2} + \dfrac{C}{3x + 2}$$

Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by $x^2(3x + 2)$:
$$3x^2 - 4 = A x(3x + 2) + B(3x + 2) + C x^2$$

Determine the constant $B$ by substituting $x = 0$:
$$3(0)^2 - 4 = A(0) + B(3(0) + 2) + C(0)^2 \implies -4 = 2B \implies B = -2$$

Determine the constant $C$ by substituting the root of $3x + 2 = 0$, which is $x = -\dfrac{2}{3}$:
$$3\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 - 4 = C\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2$$
$$3\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right) - 4 = \dfrac{4}{9}C \implies \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{12}{3} = \dfrac{4}{9}C \implies -\dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{9}C$$
$$C = -\dfrac{8}{3} \times \dfrac{9}{4} = -6$$

Determine the constant $A$ by equating coefficients of $x^2$ on both sides:
$$3 = 3A + C$$
$$3 = 3A - 6 \implies 3A = 9 \implies A = 3$$

hints: Integrate the decomposition from part (i) term by term, noting that $\int(3x+2)^{-1}dx$ introduces a factor $1/3$.
Evaluate the logarithmic and reciprocal terms at $x=1$ and $x=2$.
Combine the logarithms with product and quotient laws and simplify the rational contribution to reach the stated exact form.
walkthrough:
Substitute the partial fractions into the integral:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_1^2 \left(\dfrac{3}{x} - 2x^{-2} - \dfrac{6}{3x + 2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Write down the complete integrated expression with limits:
$$\left[3\ln x + \dfrac{2}{x} - 2\ln(3x + 2)\right]_1^2$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 2$:
$$\text{Upper limit evaluation} = 3\ln 2 + \dfrac{2}{2} - 2\ln(3(2) + 2) = 3\ln 2 + 1 - 2\ln 8$$
Since $8 = 2^3$, $2\ln 8 = 2(3\ln 2) = 6\ln 2$, so this becomes:
$$= 3\ln 2 + 1 - 6\ln 2 = 1 - 3\ln 2$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 1$:
$$\text{Lower limit evaluation} = 3\ln 1 + \dfrac{2}{1} - 2\ln(3(1) + 2) = 0 + 2 - 2\ln 5 = 2 - 2\ln 5$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = (1 - 3\ln 2) - (2 - 2\ln 5) = (2\ln 5 - 3\ln 2) - 1$$

Apply the power and quotient laws of logarithms to combine the logarithmic terms:
$$2\ln 5 - 3\ln 2 = \ln(5^2) - \ln(2^3) = \ln 25 - \ln 8 = \ln\left(\dfrac{25}{8}\right)$$

Conclude with the exact expression:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \ln\left(\dfrac{25}{8}\right) - 1$$
